aids.nom: NSSF Pension — National Social Security Fund
aids.description_en: Monthly contributory pension for formal sector workers registered with the National Social Security Fund (NSSF). Old-age pension available from age 60 after minimum 20 years of contributions. Estimated pension: KHR 150,000–1,000,000/month depending on contribution history and salary. Employee contributes 2%, employer contributes 4% of gross salary. Approximately 1.3 million formal workers covered by 2024.

aids.nom: IDPoor — Cash Transfer for Extreme Poor Households
aids.description_en: Targeted cash transfer of KHR 40,000–60,000/month for households classified as IDPoor 1 (extreme poor) or IDPoor 2 (poor) under the national poverty targeting database. IDPoor 1 households receive KHR 60,000/month; IDPoor 2 receive KHR 40,000/month. Approximately 560,000 households enrolled. IDPoor identification uses proxy means testing at commune level with 5-year cycle updates. Payments disbursed bimonthly via commune offices or mobile payment.

Monthly cash allowance of KHR 60,000 for persons with disabilities registered with MoSVY. Covers physical, sensory, and intellectual disabilities. Disability assessment by provincial health committees. Approximately 100,000 persons with disabilities registered nationally. War veterans with disabilities receive higher amounts. IDPoor-certified persons with disabilities receive priority access.
aids.organisme: Ministry of Social Affairs, Veterans and Youth Rehabilitation (MoSVY)

aids.nom: Health Equity Fund (HEF) — Free Healthcare for Poor
aids.description_en: Free access to all public health services (outpatient, inpatient, surgery, maternity) at public health facilities for IDPoor-certified households. HEF covers user fees, medicines, and transportation allowances (KHR 8,000–30,000 per visit). Operated through the Ministry of Health at 1,100+ public health facilities. Co-funded by government and development partners. Approximately 2 million poor covered. No co-payment required.
aids.organisme: Ministry of Health (MoH) / Health Equity Fund Operators

aids.description_en: Monthly scholarships from the Ministry of Education for students from IDPoor or low-income families. Lower secondary (grades 7-9): KHR 30,000/month. Upper secondary (grades 10-12): KHR 45,000/month. Technical and vocational: KHR 50,000/month. Higher education: KHR 70,000/month. Conditional on 80% attendance. Approximately 100,000 students receive scholarships.
aids.organisme: Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport (MoEYS)

aids.description_en: Maternity benefit for female workers registered with NSSF. Covers 90 days of paid maternity leave at 70% of the worker's average monthly wage. Also covers a delivery grant and medical care. Paternity leave of 10 working days for the husband. Applicable to all NSSF-registered workers in enterprises with 8+ employees.

Work injury and occupational disease compensation for NSSF-registered workers. Benefits include: full medical treatment costs, temporary disability benefit (70% of wages during recovery), permanent disability lump sum, and survivor benefit. Cambodia's garment sector (750,000+ workers) extensively covered. No worker contribution required — fully employer-funded.

In-kind rice distribution or cash equivalent for food-insecure rural households, particularly in drought-affected, flood-affected, and remote upland areas. Distributed through commune councils and implemented by MoSVY and Ministry of Agriculture in coordination with WFP. Typically 15-25 kg of rice per month or KHR 30,000–50,000 cash equivalent. Also covers IDPoor households during annual lean seasons.

aids.nom: Social Land Concession — Land for Landless Poor
aids.description_en: One-time allocation of agricultural land (typically 1-5 hectares) for landless poor families under the 2001 Land Law and 2003 Sub-Decree on Social Land Concessions. Administered by MLMUPC. Applications through commune councils. Over 15,000 families have received land since 2003. Recipients must cultivate the land for 5 years before receiving full title. Priority given to land-poor, demobilized soldiers, and displaced persons.
aids.organisme: Ministry of Land Management, Urban Planning and Construction (MLMUPC)

aids.description_en: Subsidised housing loans and grants for low-income urban households under the National Housing Policy framework. Housing loans at concessionary rates (4-6%) for amounts KHR 1,000,000–5,000,000 repayable over 10-15 years. Targets civil servants, garment workers, and low-income urban residents. Includes resettlement housing for families displaced from informal settlements in Phnom Penh and other cities.
